title: Equipment Master
context: Plant Maintenance › Preventive & Breakdown Maintenance (PM) › Equipment Master

cards.title: Database schema architecture, entity bindings, and keys of fEquipmentMaster
cards.body:
fEquipmentMaster is the foundational master maintenance interface operating within the PM module.
Header attributes map to EAM.EAMEquipmentMaster with primary key EquipmentId and EquipmentCode.
Technical specifications persist in EAM.EAMEquipmentTechDetail and EAM.EAMEquipmentBOM tables.
Supplemental attributes write to EAM.EAMEquipmentSupplementalInfo linked by EquipmentId.
Measurement parameters and alert thresholds map to EAM.EAMEquipmentMeasurementDetail in the schema.
Safety permit templates link through EAM.EAMEquipmentPermitDetail referencing PermitId.
Optimistic concurrency relies on ModifiedDate and ModifiedBy columns verified on save execution.
Custom fields interface through masterdata.customfieldssave during transaction commit.
UI grid datasets load asynchronously upon individual section selection to optimize client performance.
Foreign key constraints enforce referential integrity against location, cost center, and item master tables.
Audit triggers record modification history in EAM.EAMEquipmentAuditDetail for compliance tracking.
Atomic transaction boundaries ensure equipment headers and BOM lines commit synchronously without partial writes.
Primary keys EquipmentId and EquipmentCode maintain clustered indices to optimize lookup queries.
Foreign key relationships bind equipment records to functional locations and cost center tables.
Index seek operations ensure sub-second retrieval of asset attributes across plant maintenance queries.
Relational constraints and clustered indices optimize query execution plans during high-volume database operations.
Database triggers intercept unauthorized data manipulation attempts and enforce strict referential boundaries across schemas.

cards.title: Stored procedure bindings for search, load, save, and delete in fEquipmentMaster
cards.body:
All backend operations on fEquipmentMaster execute through specialized EAM procedures in the database.
Record searches execute through EAM.EAEMSearchData returning paginated equipment headers based on filters.
Selected equipment details load via EAM.EAEMLoadData and EAM.EAEMFillValues stored procedures.
Bill of materials persistence executes through the dedicated procedure EAM.EAEMSaveBOMDetail.
Certificate and warranty details save through the stored procedure EAM.EAEMSaveCertificateDetail.
Lot and serial reference details persist via EAM.EAEMSaveLotDetail within the save transaction.
Primary entity persistence is orchestrated by the master save routine EAM.EAEMSave.
Record deletion invokes EAM.EAEMDelete which evaluates downstream maintenance and work order references.
Dependent dropdown lookups populate dynamically using EAM.EAEMFillValuesDependent routines.
Stored procedures return structured error codes handled by the application exception layer.
All persistence procedures execute within serialized transaction blocks to maintain data consistency.
Audit logging procedures capture user credentials and execution timestamps across all master modifications.
Persistence procedures utilize table-valued parameters for efficient child record insertions.
Structured catch blocks capture relational database errors and execute explicit transaction rollbacks.
Execution plans are cached by the relational database engine to optimize throughput under heavy load.
Relational constraints and clustered indices optimize query execution plans during high-volume database operations.

cards.title: Validation logic, Boolean conditions, and error triggers in fEquipmentMaster
cards.body:
fEquipmentMaster enforces strict integrity rules prior to executing persistence routines in the database.
Empty EquipmentName or SerialNo raises an immediate validation error stopping execution on save.
YearOfManufactureDate > AcquisitionDate triggers date validation refusal.
DateOfCustody < AcquisitionDate triggers chronology validation failure.
Missing EquipmentCategory or EquipmentType dropdown selections aborts transaction processing.
DivisionId mismatch between equipment and assigned LocationId triggers division validation errors.
Duplicate EquipmentName within the same company fires duplicate name exceptions.
Negative or zero alert thresholds on measurement parameters trigger numeric validation errors.
Validation routines execute within client pre-checks and server validation procedures.
Inactive item codes selected within the bill of materials trigger item master validation errors.
All exceptions return structured error parameters mapped to localized user error notifications.
Server procedures re-verify all Boolean conditions to ensure data integrity against direct API calls.
Failed checks raise custom error codes mapped to localized user error messages in the interface.
Rollback handlers reverse all intermediate variable states when any rule triggers an exception.
Missing custodian contact details trigger structured field-level validation errors prior to database insert.
Relational constraints and clustered indices optimize query execution plans during high-volume database operations.

cards.title: Child record mutation logic, BOM persistence, and atomic transactions
cards.body:
Child record updates utilize a delete-and-reinsert pattern across secondary tables in the database.
Existing rows in EAM.EAMEquipmentBOM and measurement tables are purged on save execution.
Current UI grid rows are inserted anew within a single atomic database transaction.
If any child insertion fails, the entire transaction rolls back preserving original data.
Historical change logs capture prior equipment attributes before row replacement executes.
Concurrency timestamps prevent child replacement if another session modified the record.
Foreign key cascades verify that item codes in the BOM exist in masterdata.mItemMaster.
Audit triggers record changes in equipment physical locations to historical relocation tables.
Atomic transaction scopes guarantee that equipment attributes and BOM lines stay synchronized.
Line replacement commits synchronously with document header updates within a single transaction.
This mutation pattern prevents partial configuration saves and eliminates orphaned child records.
Transaction isolation levels prevent concurrent transactions from reading partially replaced rows.
Relational constraints and clustered indices optimize query execution plans during high-volume database operations.
Database triggers intercept unauthorized data manipulation attempts and enforce strict referential boundaries across schemas.
Transaction logs capture user connection parameters and execution timestamps to maintain comprehensive enterprise auditability.

cards.title: Referential integrity constraints and backend deletion barriers in PM
cards.body:
Backend deletion procedures evaluate foreign key dependencies across maintenance schemas in the database.
EAM.EAEMDelete queries EAM.EAMMaintenanceOrder to detect linked work orders.
The presence of linked MaintenanceRequest or MaintenanceOrder records blocks deletion.
Queries against EAM.EAMRunningHoursDetail prevent deletion if meter logs exist for the asset.
Active service contracts in EAM.EAMServiceContractDetail create blocking integrity constraints.
Permit links in EAM.EAMEquipmentPermitDetail prevent deletion while permit bindings exist.
Deletion handlers execute within explicit transaction blocks with rollback on violation.
Audit tables log deletion attempts, user credentials, and machine IP addresses.
Soft-deactivation flags Inactive are updated when assets are decommissioned from service.
Hard deletes are permitted only on unreferenced draft equipment records by administrators.
Referential integrity barriers protect historical asset maintenance logs from accidental removal.
Database triggers ensure child records in specification tables purge synchronously on draft removal.
Transaction rollback handlers ensure that partial deletions never leave orphaned records in child tables.
Audit tables log deletion attempts, user credentials, and machine IP addresses for security reviews.
Relational constraints and clustered indices optimize query execution plans during high-volume database operations.
Database triggers intercept unauthorized data manipulation attempts and enforce strict referential boundaries across schemas.
